title: The canonical functor from a pro-etale slice to the object site
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and let $W=(W\to X)$ be an object of its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. On the slice category $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], define the canonical functor $s_{X,W}:X_{\mathrm{proet}}/W\to W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by sending a triangle $(T\to X, a:T\to W)$ over $X$ to the weakly etale $W$-scheme $a:T\to W$, and a morphism of triangles to its same underlying scheme map. The arrow $a$ is weakly etale because both $T\to X$ and $W\to X$ are weakly etale. The functor keeps all underlying schemes and scheme maps unchanged.
